original_target: EP25: arbitrary strictly increasing positive moduli and arbitrary one forbidden residue per modulus, activated inclusively at m>=n_i, must the full survivor set always have logarithmic density?
scope: Theorem1 only finitely many fixed rational-affine identities q*a_i=p*n_i+c outside reciprocal-summable exception set; threshold corollary only entirely patterned class.
gap: No argument for arbitrary residues lacking finite affine patterns and no counterexample to unrestricted singleton target. Multiple residues EP486 deliberately not imported.
strictness_witness: Take n=2,3,... and a_n=floor(alpha*n) with fixed irrational alpha in(0,1). For fixed q>=1,p,c, q*a_n=p*n+c implies |(q*alpha-p)n-c|<q, so it holds only for bounded n because q*alpha-p!=0. A finite pattern collection covers only finitely many n; its complement has divergent reciprocal sum. This only proves the theorem hypothesis is strictly restrictive, not any failure of logarithmic density.
